item.title: Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September
item.content:encoded: Canadian retail sales are heading for the sharpest drop in more than a year and a half, a possible sign of cracks in the resilience of household spending and slowing momentum for the economy.

item.title: Eurozone Wage Growth Accelerates, But Remains Modest
item.content:encoded: Negotiated wage growth accelerated to 2.57% in the third quarter from 2.45% in the previous quarter, according to the ECB.

item.title: Cost Pressures Already in Pipeline to Fuel Higher Inflation
item.content:encoded: Disruptions to supply chains caused by the Middle East conflict seem set to keep inflation high well into next year even if there is a lasting agreement to end the war between the U.S. and Iran.

item.title: BOE Should Raise Key Rate to Around 5%, U.K. Economic Think Tank Says
item.content:encoded: Bank of England policymakers were set to move too slowly, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research said, urging them to raise the key rate to around 5% to tame inflation within three years.

item.title: Eurozone Inflation Rises to 4%, Driven by Energy Costs
item.content:encoded: Inflation in the eurozone reached double the European Central Bank’s target in October as energy costs continued to rise.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Climb Past Forecasts in October
item.content:encoded: The Commerce Department’s gauge of new residential construction, rose 9.9% in October to 1.309 million, compared with economists expectations of 1.25 million.

item.title: British business bank OakNorth, whose shareholders include Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners investment firm and the SoftBank Vision Fund, received a full-charter U.S. banking license
item.content:encoded: OakNorth looks across the Atlantic to lend more to growing companies.

item.title: U.K. Consumer Confidence Picks Up Despite Rising Headwinds
item.content:encoded: Consumer sentiment recovered slightly, though inflation concerns and higher interest rates are set to continue weighing on household budgets in the coming months.

item.title: Canada’s Trade Surplus Widens as Oil, Gold Drive Record Exports
item.content:encoded: The widening to C$5.35 billion in September marked the the biggest surplus in over four years as exports hit a fresh record high.

item.title: U.S. Trade Deficit Contracted in September
item.content:encoded: Imports were higher than exports by $105 billion, down 0.7% from August, in contrast to economists’ expectations for the trade gap to widen.

item.title: Home sales declined in October to their lowest level since 2010, a new trough for a housing market that has been hovering near rock bottom for more than four years
item.content:encoded: Sales of existing homes declined 5.5% from the previous month, dropping the level of sales to the lowest point since the subprime crisis period.

item.title: The Federal Reserve is limiting pay raises at its 12 regional banks to 1% next year as it seeks to rein in costs and streamline operations
item.content:encoded: Employees at the 12 regional banks were told to expect 1% annual raises, down from 3% this year.

item.title: South African Reserve Bank Maintains Main Repo Rate at 7.25%
item.content:encoded: The South African Reserve Bank maintained its main repo rate at 7.25%.

item.title: Bank of Japan’s Ueda Vows to Keep Careful Eye on Fed Moves
item.content:encoded: Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda again reiterated that he is prepared to tighten monetary policy further, reinforcing market views that another interest-rate hike could come as soon as December.

item.title: Shoppers’ complaints about food prices could soon grow louder, as surging energy costs and supply-chain delays are elevating costs for producers: “The worst is yet to come”
item.content:encoded: Grocery prices could increase again as surging energy costs and supply-chain delays are lifting costs for producers.

item.title: U.S. Consumer Mood Improved but Remained Gloomy This Month
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s preliminary November index reading was 51, up from 48 in the final October reading.

item.title: German Consumers Grow Slightly Gloomier on Lingering Inflation Concerns
item.content:encoded: The country’s consumer-climate index fell to minus 30.8 in its forecast for November, from minus 30.6 in October.

item.title: Canada Retail Sales Look to Build on August’s Rebound
item.content:encoded: Retail spending by Canadians looks to have remained on the rise last month, though the pace is showing signs of cooling as uncertainty and gasoline prices remain high.

item.title: Eurozone Goods-Trade Deficit Widens on Higher Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: The eurozone’s deficit in its trade in goods with the rest of the world continued to widen in September as households and businesses had to pay more for imports of fossil fuels.

item.title: German Trade Surplus Narrows Despite Rising Exports
item.content:encoded: German exports rebounded in September, offering some relief to manufacturers after a volatile summer, but faster growth in imports weighed on the country’s trade surplus.
